**PRE-SALE REPORT**

**Granite Peak Equipment Trust 2025-1**

**Equipment Lease Receivables-Backed Notes**

Publication Date: March 28, 2025

Clearwater Ratings Agency 55 Water Street New York, New York 10041

This excerpt is provided for the sole purpose of facilitating the closing of the transaction described herein and does not constitute a complete pre-sale report. Clearwater Ratings Agency is a nationally recognized statistical rating organization (NRSRO) registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

**Expected Ratings:**

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Class**         **Principal Amount**   **Expected Rating**   **Coupon**
  ----------------- ---------------------- --------------------- -----------------
  Class A Notes     \$308,000,000          AAA (sf)              5.25%

  Class B Notes     \$77,000,000           A (sf)                6.80%
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**[I. Transaction Overview]{.underline}**

Granite Peak Equipment Trust 2025-1 (the \"Issuer\") is a Delaware statutory trust formed on March 3, 2025, pursuant to a trust agreement between Granite Peak Capital LLC, as depositor, and Piedmont Corporate Trust Company, as owner trustee. The Issuer is issuing two classes of asset-backed notes (collectively, the \"Notes\") in an aggregate principal amount of \$385,000,000, the proceeds of which will be used to acquire a portfolio of equipment lease receivables originated by Granite Peak Capital LLC.

The Notes are being offered in two classes:

> **Class A Notes:** \$308,000,000 in aggregate principal amount, carrying an expected rating of AAA (sf) by Clearwater Ratings Agency, bearing interest at a fixed rate of 5.25% per annum (computed on the basis of a 360-day year consisting of twelve 30-day months), and having a legal final maturity date of October 15, 2030.
>
> **Class B Notes:** \$77,000,000 in aggregate principal amount, carrying an expected rating of A (sf) by Clearwater Ratings Agency, bearing interest at a fixed rate of 6.80% per annum (computed on the same basis), and having a legal final maturity date of October 15, 2031.

The Notes are secured by a portfolio of 4,287 equipment lease contracts originated by Granite Peak Capital LLC (\"Granite Peak\" or the \"Servicer\"), a Delaware limited liability company headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of \$397,412,633 as of the cutoff date of February 28, 2025 (the \"Cutoff Date\"). The equipment lease contracts are secured by a diverse mix of commercial and industrial equipment, including transportation vehicles, construction machinery, manufacturing equipment, and medical devices.

The Closing Date for the transaction is April 15, 2025. The first Payment Date is May 15, 2025. Thereafter, Payment Dates will occur on the 15th day of each calendar month (or the next succeeding business day if such day is not a business day). Interest on the Notes will accrue from the Closing Date.

The key transaction parties are as follows:

> **Owner Trustee:** Piedmont Corporate Trust Company, a Delaware banking corporation, 200 Market Street, Suite 1400, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.
>
> **Indenture Trustee:** Crestline National Bank, N.A., a national banking association, Corporate Trust Office at 600 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 2800, Atlanta, Georgia 30308.
>
> **Placement Agent:** Ridgeline Advisory Partners, 745 Fifth Avenue, 18th Floor, New York, New York 10151.
>
> **Transaction Counsel:** Hartsfield, Whitmore & Chen LLP.

Credit enhancement for the Notes is provided through a combination of: (i) initial overcollateralization of \$12,412,633, representing approximately 3.123% of the aggregate pool balance as of the Cutoff Date; (ii) a cash-funded reserve account in the initial amount of \$5,775,000, equal to 1.50% of the initial aggregate note balance; and (iii) subordination of the Class B Notes to the Class A Notes with respect to both principal and interest distributions.

**[II. Credit Enhancement and Structural Features]{.underline}**

**[II.A. Overcollateralization]{.underline}**

The initial overcollateralization amount is \$12,412,633, representing the excess of the aggregate outstanding pool balance as of the Cutoff Date (\$397,412,633) over the total initial note balance (\$385,000,000). This initial overcollateralization equals approximately 3.123% of the aggregate pool balance and provides an additional layer of credit support for the Notes beyond the reserve account and subordination mechanisms described below.

**[II.B. Reserve Account]{.underline}**

A cash-funded reserve account (Account No. 8830-4417-002) will be established at Sovereign Clearing Bank, N.A. on the Closing Date with an initial deposit of \$5,775,000, which is equal to 1.50% of the initial aggregate note balance of \$385,000,000. The reserve account will be available to cover shortfalls in interest distributions on the Class A Notes and, subject to the waterfall provisions, the Class B Notes, as well as to cover certain trust expenses. The required reserve amount steps down to 1.00% of the initial aggregate note balance (\$3,850,000) when the pool factor (the ratio of the then-current aggregate pool balance to the original aggregate pool balance) drops below 50%. At the time of such step-down, excess reserve funds of up to \$1,925,000 (being the difference between \$5,775,000 and \$3,850,000) may be released to the Distribution Account for application in accordance with the waterfall provisions set forth in Article IV of the Base Indenture.

**[II.C. Subordination]{.underline}**

The Class B Notes are fully subordinated to the Class A Notes with respect to both principal and interest distributions. The payment waterfall set forth in Section 4.02 of the Base Indenture prioritizes available funds in the following order: first, to Class A interest; second, to Class A principal (including any accelerated principal); third, to Class B interest; and fourth, to Class B principal.

**[II.D. Performance Triggers]{.underline}**

Events of Default under Section 5.04 of the Base Indenture include the following: (i) failure by the Issuer to make any required payment of interest or principal on any class of Notes within five business days following the applicable Payment Date; (ii) the monthly delinquency rate (measured as the aggregate principal balance of receivables that are 60 or more days past due, divided by the current aggregate pool balance) exceeding 6.00% for three consecutive Payment Dates; (iii) cumulative net losses exceeding 4.50% of the original aggregate pool balance, which threshold equals \$17,883,568; and (iv) the occurrence of an insolvency event with respect to the Servicer.

**[III. Account Structure and Control Requirements]{.underline}**

Clearwater has reviewed the proposed account structure for the Granite Peak Equipment Trust 2025-1 transaction. The assignment of Clearwater\'s expected ratings is conditioned on certain structural and legal requirements being satisfied at or prior to closing, including the execution and delivery of an Account Control Agreement (the \"ACA\") among the Issuer, the Servicer, the Indenture Trustee (as secured party on behalf of the noteholders), and the Securities Intermediary, which ACA must satisfy the criteria described in this Section III. Clearwater\'s review of the draft ACA and related documentation has identified the following requirements and observations.

**[III.A. Accounts]{.underline}**

Three accounts will be established and maintained at Sovereign Clearing Bank, N.A. (\"Sovereign\"), a national banking association with its principal office at 101 Federal Street, 22nd Floor, Boston, Massachusetts 02110, in each case in the name of the Issuer and subject to the security interest of the Indenture Trustee:

> 1\. **Collection Account** --- Account No. 8830-4417-001. All lease receivable collections received by or on behalf of the Servicer are to be deposited into this account within two business days of receipt. Based on the amortization schedule and expected payment patterns of the receivables portfolio, monthly collections are estimated at approximately \$8.2 million during the first 12 months following the Closing Date. The Collection Account will serve as the primary repository for all cash flows generated by the receivables pool prior to their distribution on each Payment Date.
>
> 2\. **Reserve Account** --- Account No. 8830-4417-002. This account will be funded at closing with an initial deposit of \$5,775,000, equal to 1.50% of the initial aggregate note balance of \$385,000,000. The Reserve Account will be drawn upon to cover shortfalls in interest and principal distributions as provided in the waterfall provisions of the Base Indenture.
>
> 3\. **Distribution Account** --- Account No. 8830-4417-003. Funds will be transferred from the Collection Account on the Transfer Date (defined as the second business day prior to each Payment Date) for distribution to the noteholders and other transaction parties in accordance with the waterfall provisions set forth in Article IV of the Base Indenture.

Each account will be maintained as a segregated account at Sovereign and will not be commingled with the general assets of the Issuer, the Servicer, or Sovereign.

**[III.B. Qualified Institution Requirement]{.underline}**

Each account established in connection with the transaction must be maintained at a \"Qualified Institution\" as defined in Section 3.01(c) of the Base Indenture. A Qualified Institution must satisfy the following minimum rating criteria: (i) a long-term unsecured debt rating of at least \"A\" by Clearwater Ratings Agency, and (ii) a short-term rating of at least \"A-1\" by Clearwater Ratings Agency. These requirements are designed to ensure that funds held in the accounts are maintained at an institution with sufficient creditworthiness to minimize counterparty risk.

Clearwater has confirmed that Sovereign Clearing Bank, N.A. currently satisfies the Qualified Institution criteria, holding a long-term unsecured debt rating of \"AA-\" and a short-term rating of \"A-1+\" from Clearwater. If at any time during the term of the transaction Sovereign ceases to satisfy the Qualified Institution criteria (whether as a result of a downgrade of its ratings or otherwise), the accounts must be transferred to a replacement institution that meets such criteria within 30 calendar days of the date on which Sovereign ceases to qualify. The ACA must include provisions implementing this transfer requirement, and the selection of any replacement institution is subject to the satisfaction of the Qualified Institution criteria at the time of such replacement.

**[III.C. UCC Control Requirements]{.underline}**

The ACA must establish \"control\" by the Indenture Trustee (as secured party on behalf of the noteholders) over each of the accounts described above. Clearwater requires that the ACA provide for control under Section 8-106 of the Uniform Commercial Code (the \"UCC\") with respect to each account treated as a \"securities account\" under UCC Article 8. As a practical matter, funds credited to the accounts may at any given time consist of uninvested cash balances that do not constitute \"financial assets\" under Article 8. To the extent any account holds such uninvested cash, the ACA should also address control under UCC Section 9-104 with respect to the account in its capacity as a \"deposit account\" under UCC Article 9. Clearwater notes that market-standard account control agreements for securitization transactions increasingly address both characterizations to ensure that the Indenture Trustee\'s security interest is perfected by control regardless of the nature of the assets held in the accounts at any given time. Clearwater considers this dual-characterization approach to be consistent with best practices in the structured finance market and expects that transaction counsel\'s UCC perfection opinion will address both bases for control.

**[III.D. Anti-Setoff and Lien Waiver Requirements]{.underline}**

Clearwater requires, as a condition to the assignment of its expected ratings, that the ACA include an absolute and unconditional waiver by the Securities Intermediary of any and all rights of setoff, recoupment, banker\'s lien, security interest, right of retention, counterclaim, or other right to encumber, debit, or make deductions from any funds or financial assets held in or credited to any of the Accounts (the Collection Account, the Reserve Account, and the Distribution Account, collectively the \"Accounts\"). This waiver must be comprehensive in scope and must cover all present and future claims of the Securities Intermediary, whether arising under contract, common law, statute, or regulation, including without limitation any rights arising under Sections 9-340 or 9-341 of the UCC.

The waiver must be absolute and not merely a subordination of the Securities Intermediary\'s interest to the interest of the Indenture Trustee and the noteholders. A subordination of the Securities Intermediary\'s claims to those of the Indenture Trustee and the noteholders is necessary but not sufficient; Clearwater requires a full waiver and not merely a subordination. The distinction is material: a subordination preserves the underlying right and merely alters the priority of claims, whereas a waiver extinguishes the right entirely. In the context of a rated securitization, the preservation of even a subordinated lien or setoff right by the Securities Intermediary introduces structural uncertainty that Clearwater views as inconsistent with the protections expected at the rating levels assigned to the Notes.

The Securities Intermediary must expressly acknowledge in the ACA that its claims for fees, expenses, and indemnification are unsecured general obligations of the Issuer and/or the Servicer and are not secured by any lien on, or right of setoff against, the Accounts or any funds or financial assets credited thereto. The only exception to the foregoing is that the Securities Intermediary may retain its contractual right to receive payment of agreed fees and expenses from the Issuer or the Servicer pursuant to the fee arrangements set forth in the ACA or the related fee letter; however, such contractual right does not give rise to, and shall not be construed as giving rise to, a lien, security interest, or right of setoff against the Accounts or any assets therein.

Clearwater notes that certain standard-form account control agreements utilized by depository institutions in the ordinary course of their business include provisions granting the depository bank a lien or security interest in funds held in accounts maintained at such institution to secure the payment of unpaid fees, charges, and other amounts owed by the account holder. Such provisions are inconsistent with Clearwater\'s rating criteria and must be removed or affirmatively overridden in the executed ACA for this transaction.

**[III.E. Exclusive Control Notice]{.underline}**

The ACA must include mechanics for the delivery by the Indenture Trustee of an Exclusive Control Notice upon the occurrence of an Event of Default under the Base Indenture, upon which delivery the Securities Intermediary must immediately cease complying with entitlement orders, instructions, or directions from any party other than the Indenture Trustee with respect to the Accounts. Clearwater considers the inclusion of such mechanics to be a condition to the assignment of its expected ratings, and the specific procedures governing the delivery and effectiveness of the Exclusive Control Notice should be set forth in detail in the ACA and the Base Indenture.

**[III.F. Eligible Investments]{.underline}**

Funds held in the Accounts pending distribution or application may be invested only in \"Eligible Investments\" as defined in Section 1.01 of the Base Indenture. Eligible Investments are limited to the following categories: (a) direct obligations of, or obligations the timely payment of principal and interest on which are fully guaranteed by, the United States of America, in each case maturing within 30 days of the date of investment; (b) commercial paper rated at least \"A-1+\" by Clearwater Ratings Agency (or its equivalent by another NRSRO) and maturing within 30 days of the date of investment; (c) shares of money market funds rated \"AAAm\" by Clearwater Ratings Agency; and (d) demand deposits or time deposits at any depository institution organized under the laws of the United States or any state thereof having short-term deposit ratings of at least \"A-1\" by Clearwater Ratings Agency, maturing not later than the next succeeding Transfer Date. All investment earnings on funds in an Account must be credited to the originating Account and may not be commingled across Accounts.

**[IV. Amendment and Modification Restrictions]{.underline}**

The ACA shall not be amended, modified, supplemented, or waived in any manner that could reasonably be expected to adversely affect the interests of the noteholders without at least 10 business days\' prior written notice to Clearwater Ratings Agency at the following address:

> Clearwater Ratings Agency Structured Finance Surveillance Group 55 Water Street New York, New York 10041
>
> Attention: Granite Peak Equipment Trust 2025-1 Analyst

Clearwater is not a party to the ACA and does not have a consent right with respect to any amendment or modification thereof. However, as a condition to the assignment of its expected ratings, Clearwater requires that it receive advance written notice of any proposed amendment, modification, supplement, or waiver that could reasonably be expected to adversely affect the interests of the noteholders. Such notice must include a reasonably detailed description of the proposed amendment and a copy of the proposed amendment language in substantially final form.

The failure to provide such notice to Clearwater will not, in and of itself, invalidate the amendment or render it unenforceable as among the parties to the ACA. However, the failure to provide timely notice may result in Clearwater placing its ratings on review for possible downgrade or taking other rating action as Clearwater deems appropriate in its sole discretion.

For the avoidance of doubt, administrative or ministerial amendments --- such as changes to notice addresses, corrections of typographical errors, updates to authorized signatory lists, or adjustments to fee schedules that do not increase fees payable from Account assets or otherwise alter the economic terms of the ACA --- are not considered amendments that could reasonably be expected to adversely affect the interests of the noteholders and accordingly do not require notice to Clearwater under this Section IV.

Additionally, and without limiting the foregoing, no amendment, modification, supplement, or waiver of any provision of the ACA that would alter, diminish, or otherwise affect (i) the anti-setoff and lien waiver provisions described in Section III.D of this report, (ii) the Exclusive Control Notice mechanics described in Section III.E of this report, or (iii) the Qualified Institution requirements described in Section III.B of this report may be made without at least 10 business days\' prior written notice to Clearwater at the address set forth above.

**[V. Securities Intermediary Liability and Indemnification Standards]{.underline}**

Clearwater has reviewed the standard-form account control agreement provided by Sovereign Clearing Bank, N.A. in connection with the Granite Peak Equipment Trust 2025-1 transaction. As part of its rating analysis, Clearwater considers the adequacy of the Securities Intermediary\'s liability provisions and the extent to which such provisions are consistent with the protections expected in connection with investment-grade rated securitization transactions.

Clearwater notes that the standard-form ACA provided by Sovereign includes a limitation of liability provision capping the Securities Intermediary\'s aggregate liability for all claims arising under or in connection with the ACA at an amount equal to 12 months of account maintenance fees. Based on the fee schedule provided to Clearwater, the annual account maintenance fees for the three Accounts total \$45,000 (representing \$15,000 per account per annum). Accordingly, the aggregate liability cap under the standard-form ACA would be approximately \$45,000.

Clearwater considers a liability cap of \$45,000 in connection with a \$385,000,000 securitization to be commercially inadequate and inconsistent with market practice for investment-grade rated transactions. A liability cap of this magnitude --- representing approximately 0.0117% of the aggregate note balance --- provides insufficient incentive for the Securities Intermediary to perform its obligations under the ACA with the degree of care and diligence required to support the expected ratings assigned to the Notes.

Clearwater expects that the executed ACA will address this deficiency through one or more of the following approaches: (a) removal of the liability cap in its entirety, thereby subjecting the Securities Intermediary to uncapped liability for losses arising from its acts or omissions under the ACA; (b) an increase of the liability cap to a commercially reasonable level consistent with market practice for comparable transactions, which Clearwater generally views as the greater of 12 months of fees and a minimum fixed dollar threshold that is proportionate to the transaction size; or (c) at a minimum, inclusion of a provision expressly providing that the liability cap does not apply to, and does not limit the Securities Intermediary\'s liability for, losses arising from the Securities Intermediary\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or breach of the anti-setoff and lien waiver provisions described in Section III.D of this report.

In addition, the standard-form ACA provided by Sovereign includes a broad disclaimer of consequential, incidental, special, and punitive damages, regardless of the form of action or the theory of liability. Clearwater expects that such disclaimer will be appropriately limited in the executed ACA so as not to apply to losses arising from the Securities Intermediary\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud. An unqualified disclaimer of consequential damages could, in certain circumstances, effectively immunize the Securities Intermediary from meaningful liability for losses caused by serious failures in the performance of its obligations.

The Securities Intermediary must also acknowledge in the executed ACA that its own claims for fees, expenses, and indemnification arising under the ACA are subordinated to the prior claims of the Indenture Trustee and the noteholders with respect to any funds or financial assets held in or credited to the Accounts. This subordination reinforces the structural protections described in Section III.D and ensures that the Securities Intermediary cannot assert a competing priority claim against Account assets.

**[VI. Servicer and Originator Overview]{.underline}**

Granite Peak Capital LLC is a Delaware limited liability company formed in 2011 and headquartered at 401 South Tryon Street, Suite 3200, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202. The company is led by Chief Executive Officer Marcus T. Ellison and specializes in the origination, underwriting, and servicing of commercial equipment lease contracts across a diverse range of industries. Granite Peak\'s annual origination volume has averaged approximately \$1.2 billion over the past three fiscal years.

In connection with the Granite Peak Equipment Trust 2025-1 transaction, Granite Peak will serve as both the originator of the receivables and the servicer of the receivables pool. The Servicer Fee is 0.50% per annum, calculated on a 30/360 basis on the aggregate outstanding pool balance, payable monthly in arrears on each Payment Date. Based on the aggregate outstanding pool balance as of the Cutoff Date, the first monthly Servicer Fee payment is estimated at \$165,588.60.

Under Section 7.01 of the Servicing Agreement, a \"Servicer Termination Event\" includes, among other things, the failure by the Servicer to deposit collections into the Collection Account within two business days of receipt, which failure is not cured within five business days after written notice thereof from the Indenture Trustee. Upon the occurrence and continuance of a Servicer Termination Event, the Indenture Trustee may, and at the direction of the holders of a majority of the outstanding note balance shall, terminate the Servicer and appoint a successor servicer.

**[VII. Conditions to Rating Assignment]{.underline}**

The assignment by Clearwater of its expected ratings to the Class A Notes (AAA (sf)) and the Class B Notes (A (sf)) is conditioned on the satisfaction of each of the following conditions at or prior to the Closing Date (April 15, 2025):

> 1\. Execution and delivery of the Base Indenture, dated as of the Closing Date, between the Issuer and Crestline National Bank, N.A., as Indenture Trustee, in substantially the form reviewed by Clearwater.
>
> 2\. Execution and delivery of the Servicing Agreement, dated as of the Closing Date, among the Issuer, Granite Peak Capital LLC, as Servicer, and Crestline National Bank, N.A., as Indenture Trustee, in substantially the form reviewed by Clearwater.
>
> 3\. Execution and delivery of the Account Control Agreement among the Issuer, the Servicer, Crestline National Bank, N.A. (as Indenture Trustee and Secured Party), and Sovereign Clearing Bank, N.A. (as Securities Intermediary and Depository Bank), in a form satisfying all requirements and conditions set forth in Sections III, IV, and V of this report.
>
> 4\. Establishment of the Collection Account (Account No. 8830-4417-001), the Reserve Account (Account No. 8830-4417-002), and the Distribution Account (Account No. 8830-4417-003) at Sovereign Clearing Bank, N.A., with the Reserve Account funded in the amount of \$5,775,000 on or before the Closing Date.
>
> 5\. Delivery of legal opinions from Hartsfield, Whitmore & Chen LLP, including: (a) a true-sale opinion opining that the transfer of the receivables to the Issuer constitutes a sale and not a pledge; (b) a nonconsolidation opinion opining that the assets of the Issuer would not be substantively consolidated with those of Granite Peak in a bankruptcy proceeding; and (c) a UCC perfection opinion confirming that the Indenture Trustee has a first-priority perfected security interest in the Accounts and the financial assets and funds credited thereto by virtue of \"control\" within the meaning of the applicable provisions of the UCC.
>
> 6\. Receipt by Clearwater of executed copies of the ACA and all related transaction documents in final form at least two business days prior to the Closing Date (i.e., no later than April 11, 2025).
>
> 7\. Confirmation that Sovereign Clearing Bank, N.A. satisfies the Qualified Institution criteria set forth in Section III.B as of the Closing Date.

If any of the foregoing conditions is not satisfied by the Closing Date, Clearwater reserves the right to decline to assign the expected ratings or to assign ratings different from those set forth in this report.

**[VIII. Disclaimer and Limitations]{.underline}**

This pre-sale report excerpt does not constitute, and should not be construed as, a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any security described herein. The expected ratings assigned by Clearwater are expressions of Clearwater\'s opinion regarding the creditworthiness of the rated obligations and are not recommendations regarding the suitability of any investment for any particular investor.

The expected ratings set forth in this report are based on information available to Clearwater as of the date hereof, including drafts of the transaction documents, the statistical characteristics of the receivables pool, and representations and warranties made by the transaction parties. The expected ratings are subject to change, revision, suspension, or withdrawal at any time in Clearwater\'s sole discretion and without notice.

Clearwater is not a party to the ACA, the Base Indenture, the Servicing Agreement, or any other transaction document, and has no obligation or duty to monitor the performance of the transaction, the receivables pool, or any transaction party, or to update, revise, or affirm its ratings at any time following the initial assignment thereof.

The assignment of final ratings is conditioned on Clearwater\'s receipt of final documentation substantially conforming to the drafts reviewed by Clearwater in connection with the preparation of this report and on the satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section VII above.

import re
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

def new_doc(font="Times New Roman", size=11, margins=1.0):
    d = Document()
    st = d.styles["Normal"]
    st.font.name = font
    st.font.size = Pt(size)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), font)
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    for s in d.sections:
        s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(margins)
        s.top_margin = s.bottom_margin = Inches(margins)
    return d

def add_runs(p, text, base_bold=False, base_italic=False, size=None):
    # **bold**, *italic*, __underline__
    tokens = re.split(r"(\*\*.+?\*\*|__.+?__|\*.+?\*)", text)
    for t in tokens:
        if not t:
            continue
        b, i, u = base_bold, base_italic, False
        if t.startswith("**") and t.endswith("**"):
            t = t[2:-2]; b = True
        elif t.startswith("__") and t.endswith("__"):
            t = t[2:-2]; u = True
        elif t.startswith("*") and t.endswith("*") and len(t) > 2:
            t = t[1:-1]; i = True
        r = p.add_run(t)
        r.bold = b; r.italic = i; r.underline = u
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p

def para(d, text, align="j", indent=0.0, first=0.0, bold=False, italic=False, size=None, after=6, before=0, keep=False):
    p = d.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text, bold, italic, size)
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    pf.alignment = {"j": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY, "c": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, "l": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT, "r": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT}[align]
    if indent: pf.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    if first: pf.first_line_indent = Inches(first)
    pf.space_after = Pt(after); pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep: pf.keep_with_next = True
    return p

def page_break(d):
    p = d.add_paragraph()
    p.add_run().add_break(WD_BREAK.PAGE)

def shade(cell, color="D9D9D9"):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"), color)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def table(d, rows, widths, header=True, size=10):
    t = d.add_table(rows=len(rows), cols=len(rows[0]))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        for ci, val in enumerate(row):
            c = t.cell(ri, ci)
            c.width = Inches(widths[ci])
            c.text = ""
            p = c.paragraphs[0]
            add_runs(p, val, base_bold=(header and ri == 0), size=size)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            if header and ri == 0: shade(c)
    d.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def footer_page_numbers(d, label=""):
    for s in d.sections:

import re
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

def new_doc(font="Times New Roman", size=11, margins=1.0):
    d = Document()
    st = d.styles["Normal"]
    st.font.name = font
    st.font.size = Pt(size)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), font)
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    for s in d.sections:
        s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(margins)
        s.top_margin = s.bottom_margin = Inches(margins)
    return d

def add_runs(p, text, base_bold=False, base_italic=False, size=None):
    # **bold**, *italic*, __underline__
    tokens = re.split(r"(\*\*.+?\*\*|__.+?__|\*.+?\*)", text)
    for t in tokens:
        if not t:
            continue
        b, i, u = base_bold, base_italic, False
        if t.startswith("**") and t.endswith("**"):
            t = t[2:-2]; b = True
        elif t.startswith("__") and t.endswith("__"):
            t = t[2:-2]; u = True
        elif t.startswith("*") and t.endswith("*") and len(t) > 2:
            t = t[1:-1]; i = True
        r = p.add_run(t)
        r.bold = b; r.italic = i; r.underline = u
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    return p

def para(d, text, align="j", indent=0.0, first=0.0, bold=False, italic=False, size=None, after=6, before=0, keep=False):
    p = d.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text, bold, italic, size)
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    pf.alignment = {"j": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY, "c": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER, "l": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT, "r": WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT}[align]
    if indent: pf.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    if first: pf.first_line_indent = Inches(first)
    pf.space_after = Pt(after); pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep: pf.keep_with_next = True
    return p

def page_break(d):
    p = d.add_paragraph()
    p.add_run().add_break(WD_BREAK.PAGE)

def shade(cell, color="D9D9D9"):

    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")

P("(a) The Securities Intermediary hereby agrees that (i) each Account is and shall be maintained as a “securities account” within the meaning of Section 8-501(a) of the UCC; (ii) it is acting as a “securities intermediary” (within the meaning of Section 8-102(a)(14) of the UCC) with respect to each Account; (iii) the Issuer is the sole “entitlement holder” (within the meaning of Section 8-102(a)(7) of the UCC) with respect to each Account; and (iv) all Account Property (other than uninvested cash to the extent treated as a credit balance in a Deposit Account pursuant to Section 2.3) shall be treated as a “financial asset” within the meaning of Section 8-102(a)(9) of the UCC.")
P("(b) All securities, instruments and other property underlying any Financial Asset credited to any Account shall be registered in the name of the Securities Intermediary or its nominee, indorsed to the Securities Intermediary or in blank, or credited to another securities account maintained in the name of the Securities Intermediary (including at a clearing corporation or Federal Reserve Bank), and in no case shall any Financial Asset credited to any Account be registered in the name of the Issuer or the Servicer, payable to the order of the Issuer or the Servicer, or specially indorsed to the Issuer or the Servicer, except to the extent the foregoing have been specially indorsed to the Securities Intermediary or in blank.")

No characterization of any Account Property under either Article 8 or Article 9 of the UCC shall limit or impair the Indenture Trustee’s control under the other.")
S("2.4 Securities Intermediary’s Jurisdiction; Bank’s Jurisdiction; Governing Law of Accounts.")
P("(a) The Parties hereby expressly agree, as a deliberate contractual election pursuant to Section 8-110(e)(1) of the UCC, that the State of New York is the “securities intermediary’s jurisdiction” with respect to each Account for purposes of Part 1 of Article 8 of the UCC, Article 8 of the UCC and the UCC generally (including Section 9-305(a)(3) of the UCC). P("(b) The Parties hereby expressly agree, pursuant to Section 9-304(b)(1) of the UCC, that the State of New York is the “bank’s jurisdiction” with respect to each Account, to the extent any Account constitutes a Deposit Account, for purposes of Part 3 of Article 9 of the UCC, Article 9 of the UCC and the UCC generally.")
P("(c) This Agreement constitutes, and the Parties agree that it shall be part of, the agreement between the Securities Intermediary and the Issuer governing each Account, and the Parties agree that the law of the State of New York governs each Account and all issues relating thereto. For purposes of the Convention on the Law Applicable to Certain Rights in Respect of Securities Held with an Intermediary (the “**Hague Securities Convention**”), the Parties agree that the law of the State of New York shall govern all issues specified in Article 2(1) of the Hague Securities Convention, and the Securities Intermediary represents and warrants that, at the time of execution of this Agreement, it has an office in the United States (including its office at 101 Federal Street, Boston, Massachusetts) that satisfies the requirements of Article 4(1) of the Hague Securities Convention.")
P("(d) Neither this Section 2.4 nor the jurisdiction elections herein may be amended except in accordance with Section 15, and no Account Agreement shall designate any other jurisdiction as the securities intermediary’s jurisdiction or the bank’s jurisdiction with respect to any Account.")
S("2.5 Representations as to Accounts.")
P("The Securities Intermediary represents and warrants that (a) Schedule A accurately describes each Account; (b) it has not received notice of any lien, security interest, adverse claim (within the meaning of Section 8-102(a)(1) of the UCC), garnishment, levy, attachment or other legal process with respect to any Account or Account Property other than the security interest of the Indenture Trustee; and (c) it has not entered into, and covenants that it will not enter into, any agreement with any Person (other than the Indenture Trustee hereunder) pursuant to which it has agreed or would agree to comply with Instructions of such Person with respect to any Account or Account Property, or otherwise to give any Person other than the Indenture Trustee “control” over any Account or Account Property.")

from aca_part1 import *

H("SECTION 3. CONTROL; INSTRUCTIONS")
S("3.1 Control over Securities Accounts (UCC Section 8-106).")
P("The Securities Intermediary hereby agrees that it shall comply with all Entitlement Orders originated by the Indenture Trustee with respect to each Account and the Financial Assets and security entitlements credited thereto, without further consent by the Issuer, the Servicer or any other Person. This agreement is intended to and shall constitute an agreement for purposes of Section 8-106(d)(2) of the UCC.")
S("3.2 Control over Deposit Accounts (UCC Section 9-104).")
P("The Securities Intermediary, in its capacity as bank, hereby agrees that it shall comply with all Instructions originated by the Indenture Trustee directing the disposition of funds in each Account (to the extent such Account constitutes a Deposit Account) without further consent by the Issuer, the Servicer or any other Person. This agreement is intended to and shall constitute an agreement for purposes of Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC.")
S("3.3 Indenture Trustee Authority Paramount.")
P("The Indenture Trustee may originate Instructions with respect to any Account at any time, whether before or after the delivery of an Exclusive Control Notice. If at any time the Securities Intermediary receives conflicting Instructions from the Indenture Trustee and from the Servicer, the Issuer or any other Person, the Securities Intermediary shall comply with the Instructions of the Indenture Trustee and shall not comply with the conflicting Instructions. The Securities Intermediary shall have no liability to the Issuer, the Servicer or any other Person for complying with Instructions of the Indenture Trustee in accordance with this Agreement. The Issuer and the Servicer acknowledge that neither of them has any right to give Instructions with respect to any Account except as expressly set forth in Section 3.4, and that such rights are subordinate to the rights of the Indenture Trustee hereunder.")
S("3.4 Servicer Instructions Prior to an Exclusive Control Notice.")
P("(a) Until the Securities Intermediary receives an Exclusive Control Notice (and after the Securities Intermediary receives a Revocation Notice, until it receives any subsequent Exclusive Control Notice), the Securities Intermediary shall comply with Instructions originated by an Authorized Person of the Servicer, acting on behalf of the Issuer, solely of the following types, as permitted by Section 3.01(b) of the Indenture and Sections 4.01 and 4.03 of the Servicing Agreement (each, a “**Permitted Servicer Instruction**”):")
B("(i) Instructions to invest and reinvest funds in any Account in Eligible Investments in accordance with Section 4;")
B("(ii) Instructions to transfer Available Funds from the Collection Account to the Distribution Account on or in respect of a Transfer Date, which Instructions the Servicer shall deliver not later than 12:00 noon (New York City time) on the Business Day immediately preceding such Transfer Date in accordance with Section 3.02(c) of the Indenture;")
B("(iii) Instructions to withdraw from the Collection Account and pay to the Servicer the Servicer Fee in accordance with Section 4.03(b) of the Servicing Agreement, delivered no earlier than two Business Days prior to, and not later than 12:00 noon (New York City time) on, the applicable Payment Date;")
B("(iv) Reserve Release Certificates delivered in accordance with Section 6; and")
B("(v) such other Instructions with respect to the Accounts as are expressly permitted to be given by the Servicer under the Indenture and the Servicing Agreement and are countersigned by an Authorized Person of the Indenture Trustee.")
P("(b) Neither the Issuer (other than through the Servicer as provided above) nor the Servicer shall have any right to originate any other Instruction, and the Securities Intermediary shall not comply with (i) any Instruction from the Issuer or the Owner Trustee (other than an Instruction countersigned by the Indenture Trustee), or (ii) any Instruction from the Servicer that, on its face, directs a transfer or payment of Account Property to any account or Person other than another Account, except for payment of the Servicer Fee from the Collection Account under clause (a)(iii) above. Any Instruction from the Servicer that is not a Permitted Servicer Instruction shall be void and of no effect for purposes of this Agreement (consistent with Section 4.03(d) of the Servicing Agreement). The Securities Intermediary shall promptly (and in any event within one Business Day) notify the Indenture Trustee of its receipt of any Instruction it has declined to execute under this Section 3.4(b).")
P("(c) The Securities Intermediary shall not be required to verify whether the conditions precedent to a Permitted Servicer Instruction under the Indenture or the Servicing Agreement (including the delivery of a Monthly Servicer Report or the absence of an Event of Default) have been satisfied, except as expressly set forth in Section 6. Nothing in this Section 3.4 shall be construed to limit or impair the Indenture Trustee’s rights under Sections 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3.")
S("3.5 Indenture Trustee Withdrawals and Distributions.")
P("Withdrawals from the Reserve Account to cover shortfalls pursuant to Section 3.03(b) of the Indenture and distributions from the Distribution Account in accordance with the Priority of Payments shall be made solely upon Instructions of the Indenture Trustee (it being understood that the Indenture Trustee may deliver a single Instruction covering all distributions on a Payment Date). The Securities Intermediary shall make each such withdrawal, transfer or distribution in immediately available funds on the date specified in the applicable Instruction, provided such Instruction is received by 12:00 noon (New York City time) on the Business Day prior to such date (or such later time as the Securities Intermediary may accommodate).")
S("3.6 Account Property Not Subject to Other Instructions.")
P("Except as provided in this Section 3 and in Sections 4, 5 and 6, the Securities Intermediary shall not permit any withdrawal, transfer, payment or other disposition of any Account Property.")
S("3.7 Reliance; Security Procedures.")
P("Instructions may be delivered in writing (including by electronic mail transmitting a signed portable document format (.pdf) copy, or through an electronic platform of the Securities Intermediary subject to commercially reasonable security procedures agreed in writing by the Securities Intermediary, the Servicer and the Indenture Trustee). The Securities Intermediary may rely, without independent inquiry, on any Instruction or notice that it believes in good faith to be genuine and to have been signed or sent by an Authorized Person of the Indenture Trustee or, subject to Section 3.4 and Section 5, the Servicer, and that has been verified in accordance with such security procedures; *provided* that the Securities Intermediary shall not, after receipt of an Exclusive Control Notice, rely upon or comply with any Instruction of the Servicer or the Issuer.")
S("3.8 Authorized Persons.")
P("Schedule D sets forth the Authorized Persons of the Servicer and of the Indenture Trustee as of the Closing Date. The Servicer may update its Authorized Persons only by written notice to the Securities Intermediary signed by an existing Authorized Person of the Servicer, with a concurrent copy to the Indenture Trustee, and the Indenture Trustee may update its Authorized Persons by written notice signed by an existing Authorized Person of the Indenture Trustee. No update to Schedule D shall expand the types of Instructions that may be given by the Servicer. Following delivery of an Exclusive Control Notice, the Authorized Persons of the Servicer shall have no authority hereunder.")

H("SECTION 4. INVESTMENT OF ACCOUNT FUNDS")
S("4.1 Bifurcated Investment Authority.")
P("(a) **Prior to an Exclusive Control Notice.** Until the Securities Intermediary receives an Exclusive Control Notice (and following receipt of a Revocation Notice), the Servicer shall have authority, pursuant to Section 4.01(b)(i) of the Servicing Agreement and Section 6.01 of the Indenture, to instruct the Securities Intermediary in writing to invest and reinvest funds on deposit in each Account in Eligible Investments; *provided* that the Indenture Trustee may also give investment Instructions at any time and, in the event of conflict, Section 3.3 shall apply.")
P("(b) **Following an Exclusive Control Notice.** From and after the Securities Intermediary’s receipt of an Exclusive Control Notice (and until receipt of a Revocation Notice), the Indenture Trustee shall have sole and exclusive authority to instruct the Securities Intermediary with respect to the investment and reinvestment of funds in each Account, and the Securities Intermediary shall not comply with any investment Instruction from the Servicer, the Issuer or any other Person, consistent with Section 4.01(b)(ii) of the Servicing Agreement and Section 6.01 of the Indenture. Any Eligible Investment made pursuant to a Servicer Instruction prior to such receipt may be held to maturity unless the Indenture Trustee otherwise instructs.")
P("(c) Investment Instructions shall be delivered not later than 12:00 noon (New York City time) on the Business Day on which the investment is to be made, as provided in Section 6.01 of the Indenture, and shall specify the Account from which the investment is to be made. Each investment Instruction shall be deemed to include a representation by the Person giving it that the investment directed constitutes an Eligible Investment and matures or is redeemable at par not later than the Business Day immediately preceding the next Payment Date (or such earlier date as is required by the Transaction Documents).")
S("4.2 Eligible Investments Only; No Discretionary Sweep.")
P("The Securities Intermediary shall invest Account Property only as directed in Instructions given in accordance with Section 4.1 and shall not invest any Account Property in any investment that it knows is not an Eligible Investment. In the absence of timely investment Instructions, funds in each Account shall remain uninvested as a cash credit balance in such Account (constituting, to the extent provided in Section 2.3, funds in a Deposit Account subject to the Indenture Trustee’s control under Section 3.2), or, if the Securities Intermediary is then a Qualified Institution and the Servicer (or, after an Exclusive Control Notice, the Indenture Trustee) has so directed by standing Instruction, shall be held in demand deposits at the Securities Intermediary, in each case as contemplated by Section 6.01 of the Indenture. The Securities Intermediary shall not invest any Account Property in any overnight sweep vehicle, money market fund or other investment product of the Securities Intermediary or any of its affiliates in the absence of a written Instruction specifying such investment and confirming that it is an Eligible Investment. Neither the Securities Intermediary nor the Indenture Trustee shall have liability for lost investment income resulting from the absence of timely investment Instructions.")
S("4.3 Responsibility for Eligibility.")
P("Consistent with Section 4.01(b)(iv) of the Servicing Agreement, the Servicer (or, following an Exclusive Control Notice, the Indenture Trustee) is responsible for determining that each investment it directs is an Eligible Investment, and the Securities Intermediary shall have no duty to monitor or verify such eligibility; *provided* that nothing in this Section 4.3 shall relieve the Securities Intermediary of its obligations under Sections 4.2 and 4.4 or of liability for its own negligence, bad faith, willful misconduct or fraud.")
S("4.4 Crediting of Investment Earnings; Prohibition on Commingling.")
P("(a) In accordance with Section 6.02 of the Indenture and Section 4.01(b)(iii) of the Servicing Agreement, all interest, dividends, gains, income, investment earnings and proceeds of, and all principal and maturity proceeds of, each Eligible Investment made with funds from a particular Account shall be credited by the Securities Intermediary to that same originating Account promptly upon receipt or maturity, and in any event on the Business Day of receipt. Under no circumstances shall the Securities Intermediary credit, transfer, commingle or otherwise apply any such earnings or proceeds to or with any other Account or any other account or property. Any losses realized on any Eligible Investment shall be charged solely against the Account from which such investment was made.")

H("SECTION 6. RESERVE ACCOUNT; STEP-DOWN AND RELEASE MECHANICS")
S("6.1 Funding; Restrictions on Withdrawals.")
P("On the Closing Date the Issuer shall cause the Initial Required Reserve Amount of $5,775,000 to be deposited into the Reserve Account, and the Securities Intermediary shall confirm the credit thereof to the Indenture Trustee and the Servicer on the Closing Date. Funds in the Reserve Account shall be withdrawn only (a) to cover shortfalls upon Instructions of the Indenture Trustee in accordance with Section 3.03(b) of the Indenture, (b) to release excess amounts to the Distribution Account in accordance with this Section 6, or (c) otherwise upon Instructions of the Indenture Trustee. Investment earnings on the Reserve Account shall remain in the Reserve Account in accordance with Section 4.4 and Section 6.02 of the Indenture.")
S("6.2 Reserve Step-Down Certification.")
P("If, on any Determination Date, the Servicer determines that the Pool Factor is less than 50%, then, in order to effect the release of the excess over the Reduced Required Reserve Amount in accordance with Section 3.03(c) of the Indenture, the Servicer (acting on behalf of the Issuer) may deliver to the Securities Intermediary, with a concurrent copy to the Indenture Trustee, a Reserve Release Certificate that:")
B("(a) certifies the Pool Factor as of the last day of the related Collection Period (calculated against the Cutoff Date pool balance of $397,412,633) and that such Pool Factor is less than 50%;")
B("(b) certifies that the Monthly Servicer Report for the related Collection Period, containing such calculation and the certification required by Section 3.03(c)(ii) of the Indenture, has been delivered to the Indenture Trustee, and attaches a copy of the relevant page(s) thereof;")
B("(c) certifies that, to the Servicer’s knowledge, no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing and no Exclusive Control Notice is in effect;")
B("(d) specifies the amount to be released (the “**Release Amount**”), which shall equal the amount on deposit in the Reserve Account as of the related Transfer Date (after giving effect to any withdrawal for the related Payment Date under Section 3.03(b) of the Indenture) minus the Reduced Required Reserve Amount of $3,850,000 (which, if the Reserve Account is then funded at the Initial Required Reserve Amount, equals $1,925,000); and")
B("(e) specifies the related Transfer Date and Payment Date.")
S("6.3 Indenture Trustee Objection Right.")
P("The Indenture Trustee may, by written notice to the Securities Intermediary (with a copy to the Servicer) delivered not later than 12:00 noon (New York City time) on the Business Day immediately preceding the related Transfer Date (a “**Release Objection Notice**”), object to any Reserve Release Certificate for any reason, including that it has issued or intends to issue a contrary notice, that it disputes the Pool Factor calculation or Release Amount, or that an Event of Default has occurred. The Indenture Trustee may alternatively confirm in writing that it has no objection, in which case the Securities Intermediary may effect the release on the related Transfer Date without awaiting expiry of the objection period. The Indenture Trustee shall have no duty to recalculate the Pool Factor and may rely on the Monthly Servicer Report as provided in Section 4.02(c) of the Servicing Agreement.")
S("6.4 Release and Transfer.")
P("(a) Provided that (i) the Securities Intermediary has received a Reserve Release Certificate not later than 12:00 noon (New York City time) on the third Business Day preceding the related Transfer Date, (ii) the Securities Intermediary has not received a Release Objection Notice by the deadline set forth in Section 6.3 (or has received the Indenture Trustee’s written confirmation of no objection), and (iii) the Securities Intermediary has not received an Exclusive Control Notice that remains unrevoked, the Securities Intermediary shall, on the related Transfer Date, transfer the Release Amount from the Reserve Account to the Distribution Account (Account No. 8830-4417-003), for inclusion in Available Funds and application on the related Payment Date in accordance with the Priority of Payments. If a Reserve Release Certificate is received after such deadline, the release shall be effected on the next succeeding Transfer Date (subject to the same conditions) unless the Indenture Trustee instructs an earlier transfer.")
P("(b) The Securities Intermediary shall not transfer any Release Amount to any account other than the Distribution Account, and shall not transfer any amount that would reduce the balance of the Reserve Account below $3,850,000 (and, if the Release Amount specified exceeds such limit, shall transfer only the permitted amount and notify the Servicer and the Indenture Trustee).")
P("(c) Following receipt of an Exclusive Control Notice, the Servicer may not deliver a Reserve Release Certificate, and releases from the Reserve Account shall be made solely upon Instructions of the Indenture Trustee in accordance with Section 3.03 of the Indenture.")
S("6.5 No Reversion; Other Excess Releases.")
P("Consistent with Section 3.03(c) of the Indenture, once a Reserve Step-Down has been effected, the Required Reserve Amount shall remain at $3,850,000 for the remaining term of the Notes, and no subsequent increase in the Pool Factor shall cause it to revert to $5,775,000. Any other release of amounts on deposit in the Reserve Account in excess of the then-applicable Required Reserve Amount pursuant to Section 3.03(a) of the Indenture shall be effected only to the Distribution Account and only in accordance with the procedures of Sections 6.2 through 6.4 (*mutatis mutandis*) or upon Instructions of the Indenture Trustee. The Securities Intermediary shall have no duty to monitor the Pool Factor or the Required Reserve Amount.")

H("SECTION 7. WAIVER OF SETOFF, RECOUPMENT AND LIENS")
S("7.1 Absolute Waiver.")
P("The Securities Intermediary hereby irrevocably, absolutely and unconditionally waives, releases and relinquishes, and agrees that it does not have and shall not assert or exercise, any security interest, lien (including any banker’s lien), right of setoff, right of recoupment, right of retention, counterclaim, deduction or other right or claim to encumber, debit, charge, withhold or make deductions from any Account or any Account Property, whether now existing or hereafter arising, and whether arising under contract (including any Account Agreement), common law, statute, regulation or otherwise, including any rights under Sections 4-210, 8-511, 9-340 or 9-341 of the UCC or under any comparable law. This waiver is a waiver and extinguishment of such rights and not merely a subordination thereof. The standard-form lien for fees and expenses previously proposed by the Securities Intermediary is not part of this Agreement, and the Securities Intermediary shall not debit any Account for any fees, charges, expenses, indemnities, overdrafts, advances or other amounts owing to it.")
S("7.2 Fee and Indemnity Claims Unsecured.")
P("The Securities Intermediary acknowledges and agrees that all of its claims for fees, expenses, indemnification and other amounts arising under this Agreement or any Account Agreement are unsecured general obligations of the Servicer (and, to the limited extent provided in Section 11.6, the Issuer) and are not secured by any lien on, or right of setoff against, any Account or Account Property. The Securities Intermediary’s contractual right to receive payment of fees and expenses pursuant to Section 10 and Schedule C does not give rise to, and shall not be construed as giving rise to, any lien, security interest or right of setoff against any Account or Account Property.")
S("7.3 Subordination Acknowledgment.")
P("Without limiting Section 7.1, to the extent that any claim of the Securities Intermediary against the Issuer is, notwithstanding Section 7.1, determined to give rise to any interest in any Account or Account Property, the Securities Intermediary agrees that such claim and interest are subordinate in all respects to the security interest and claims of the Indenture Trustee and the Noteholders, and that the Securities Intermediary shall hold any Account Property received in violation of Section 7.1 in trust for the Indenture Trustee and immediately restore it to the applicable Account. This Section 7.3 is supplemental to, and shall not be construed to limit, qualify or condition, the absolute waiver in Section 7.1.")
S("7.4 Overdrafts; Returned Items.")
P("The Securities Intermediary shall not be required to make any advance or permit any overdraft in any Account, and shall not execute any Instruction to the extent there are insufficient available funds in the applicable Account. The Securities Intermediary may reverse a provisional credit for an item deposited to an Account that is returned unpaid only if such reversal is effected before the credited funds have been disbursed from such Account; otherwise its recourse for returned items shall be solely against the Servicer as an unsecured claim.")
S("7.5 Condition Precedent; No Modification.")
P("The Parties acknowledge that the inclusion of this Section 7 is a condition precedent to the execution and delivery of this Agreement under Section 3.01(e) of the Indenture and a condition to Clearwater’s assignment of its ratings to the Notes. Neither the Issuer nor the Servicer shall consent to any amendment or waiver that would eliminate, limit or otherwise modify this Section 7 without the prior written consent of the Indenture Trustee and compliance with Section 15.")

H("SECTION 8. REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS")
S("8.1 Securities Intermediary.")
